name: WCA Cube Solving
fullName: WCA cube solving: restore a scrambled 3x3x3 cube under a move budget

actions.finish: Declare the attempt complete, ending the episode for the solved-state check.
actions.turn: Apply a sequence of one to twenty moves in WCA notation: face moves F, B, R, L, U, D with ' and 2 modifiers, and whole-cube rotations x, y, z which count as zero moves.

evaluation.efficiency: Moves used in the Outer Block Turn Metric, reported with the scramble depth and with the optimal solution length computed by the host for the instance.
evaluation.failure: The cube is not solved at finish, or the 60-action or 300-move budget is exhausted; this corresponds to a DNF.
evaluation.success: When the episode ends the cube is in the solved state: every face shows a single colour, in any orientation, within at most 300 moves in the Outer Block Turn Metric.

assignment.generation: Each instance applies a scramble to a solved cube. The difficulty knob is the scramble: random face-move sequences of depth 3, 5, 7, 10 or 14 without immediately cancelling moves, plus random-state scrambles generated by the official WCA scramble program. Shallow scrambles can be undone by careful reasoning and are usually solved, while random-state scrambles require a full solving method and usually fail, so outcomes are mixed. The scramble sequence and seed are stored.
assignment.observation: A text net of all 54 stickers (six 3x3 faces labelled U, R, F, D, L, B with one colour letter per sticker), the number of moves used in the Outer Block Turn Metric, and the remaining budget. No solver hints are given.
assignment.reference: Self-proposed virtual 3x3x3 cube attempt built on the WCA Regulations: scramble sequences applied to a solved cube (Article 4), face moves in WCA notation (Regulation 12a1), move counting in the Outer Block Turn Metric (12a5), and the solved-state definition with any final orientation (Article 10). New designs: the facelet observation, the stepwise move interface, the scramble-depth ladder, the move budget and the trajectory recorder.
assignment.task: Restore a scrambled 3x3x3 cube to the solved state by applying face turns in WCA notation, observing the cube after every batch of turns, within a move budget.
assignment.verification: The host replays the scramble and every submitted move from the solved cube and checks the final state, which reproduces the Fewest Moves correctness rule. Each episode records the scramble, every action with its move sequence, the resulting sticker state and the running move count, and the terminal verdict, for successful and failed attempts.

notes: Nine newly seeded synthetic random-depth scrambles: three each at depths 3, 5 and 7. These are local reconstruction instances, not official TNoodle random-state samples. Each actual 54-facelet state differs from every original and every other new state.

instances.json replaces all old embedded scrambles. referenceFacelets were computed with the unchanged local 54-sticker engine; they are not claimed as external TNoodle verification. optimalLength is exact OBTM for these shallow scrambles, certified by exhaustive bidirectional breadth-first search (solved side depth 3, target side through depth 4).

All six face moves and their inverse/double variants are searched with only consecutive-same-face pruning; free cube rotations cannot shorten a face-turn solution because conjugating face turns moves rotations to the end. Actual optimal solutions are executed and checked through the unchanged task scorer.
